user_statement: Please note the faucet display cover has been proven solid and successful, those broad long thin (but not too thin!) walls provide the necessary give and spring, more so than anything else anyone else has tried, in PET-GF so far.
design_precedent: Simple broad, substantial side walls provide the elastic give and spring, with broad retaining lips. This complete cover is Derek’s sole accepted example for the snap-fit design approach.
scope: Derek confirms the existing faucet cover. A newly proportioned keeper or spring capture must establish its own physical fit and retention; force and cycle-life values have not been measured.
user_design_feedback: Please don’t consider that “it fit well” reason to use that design or any part of it. Please consider I prefer simplicity and the previous design and the remaining half still seem overly complicated to me. Please consider I don’t love the nameplate for its complexity, and the faucet display cover is the only one that has been simple enough, with thick enough and broad enough components for the snap.

current_geometry_result.status: Approved normal assembly and appearance with accepted remaining front-corner gap
current_geometry_result.scope: The identified black cover on the lowered tip with switch pockets is approved. The remaining visible corner gap is accepted as good enough; no further iteration is requested. Numerical force and lifetime are unmeasured.

prior_geometry_results.status: Accepted with part cooling off for normal assembly
prior_geometry_results.scope: Acceptance belongs to the identified pre-clearance-change STL. The display-clearance revision requires its own physical result.
